01.actor: The daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon; the Sages
01.event: The Sages apportion her a huge wine allowance from her late husband's estate
01.turn: She blesses them that their daughters receive the same
01.outcome: Knowing she was a widow awaiting levirate marriage, they refuse to answer amen
01.summary: After Nakdimon ben Guryon's son died, the Sages awarded his widow two se'a of wine a week for pudding. In gratitude she blessed them that their own daughters should be awarded the same. Because she was a widow waiting for her yavam, they did not answer amen, not wishing her fate on their daughters.
01.reason: An apportioning act by the court, the widow's response, and the Sages' pointed refusal give several actions and a turn beyond a bare ruling; R-C0 allows incident plus ruling when more happens.

02.actor: Rav Avya and the sister of Rami bar Hama
02.missing: The passage states only a marriage; the lost ketubah and the visit to Rav Yosef are in the following context.
02.reason: Taken alone the passage is a single background fact with no event; whatever story there is lies outside it.

03.missing: Any one-time event; only his habitual enigmatic phrasing is given.
03.reason: A habitual manner of speech that leads to nothing is a custom and speech, not a story.

04.event: Walking on the road behind a woman, Rav urges Rav Yehuda to hurry away from her
04.turn: Rav Yehuda objects with Rav's own ruling; Rav says it applies only to men like R. Hanina bar Pappi
04.outcome: Implied: they hurry on; the exchange ends with Rav's self-deprecating clarification
04.summary: Rav and Rav Yehuda were walking and a woman was walking ahead of them. Rav told Rav Yehuda to hurry away from Gehenna. Rav Yehuda cited Rav's own leniency for men of fit morals, and Rav answered that it applied to people like R. Hanina bar Pappi, not to them.
04.missing: An explicit action after the dialogue; the hurrying is only implied.
04.reason: There is a real situation (walking behind the woman) but the passage is mainly dialogue with implied action, R-C7 shape 1.

05.actor: A certain man and a woman washing her feet
05.event: He snatches coins from another man and throws them to her, declaring her betrothed
05.turn: The matter is brought before Rava
05.outcome: Rava rules the stolen coins do not effect betrothal
05.summary: A woman was washing her feet when a man grabbed dinars from someone else, threw them to her, and declared her betrothed to him. The case came before Rava, who ruled that no one follows R. Shimon on robbery, so the betrothal with stolen money fails.
05.reason: Matches R-C0's cow case: a narrated wrongful act (stealing and throwing the coins, betrothing) followed by a rabbi's ruling.

06.event: A man let witnesses trace their names on ordinary documents
06.summary: A man applied the tracing leniency to ordinary documents, and Rav Kahana had him flogged for it.
06.missing: Any detail of the incident; it is cited in one line as a precedent.
06.reason: A real act and a punitive response are reported, but only as a one-line precedent with almost nothing narrated; between borderline and not, borderline.

07.missing: Any event beyond coming before the rabbi and the rabbi's reply with a parable.
07.reason: Coming before a rabbi is the only event, followed by speech and a parable, with no conflict or change (R-C0's limit).

08.actor: A herdsman of orphans' cattle; a creditor
08.event: The creditor seized an ox from the herdsman
08.turn: They dispute whether it was before or after the debtor's death and come before Rav Nahman
08.outcome: Rav Nahman rules for the creditor by migo
08.summary: A creditor seized an ox from the herdsman caring for orphans' cattle. The two disputed whether the seizure preceded the debtor's death and came before Rav Nahman, who asked for witnesses and, there being none, ruled the creditor credible.
08.missing: Any action or change after the ruling.
08.reason: There is a real event (the seizure) and a dispute, but then only questioning and a ruling; closer to one event then ruling, yet the seizure is more than merely coming to court, so borderline.

09.event: During a famine the Sages ask Rav Yosef to pray
09.summary: In Rav Yosef's years there was a famine. The Sages asked him to pray for mercy, and he refused, arguing that Elisha, who supported thousands of scholars, did not pray in a time of wrath.
09.missing: What happened afterwards; the passage ends in dialogue.
09.reason: A real situation (famine) frames a request and refusal with some conflict, but the passage is mainly speech.

10.event: He habitually sends four dinars to a pauper; one day sends them by his wife
10.turn: She returns saying the man does not need charity, having overheard talk of fine dining
10.outcome: The resolution (Rabbi Hanina's response) follows in the next segment
10.summary: Rabbi Hanina used to send four dinars to a poor man every Shabbat eve. One day he sent them with his wife, who came back saying the man did not need it, because she had overheard his household asking which tablecloths he dined on.
10.missing: Rabbi Hanina's reaction, which lies in the context.
10.reason: A habit followed by a one-time event with a discovery and turn (R-C3); the passage carries the story's core even if its close is in the next segment.

11.missing: The passage breaks off mid-claim; the man's answer and the ruling are in the context.
11.reason: Coming before a rabbi with claims is the only event, and the passage contains nothing further.

12.missing: Any narrated event; this is exegetical calculation of dates.
12.reason: A scriptural derivation of Moses' birth and death dates is exegesis about a biblical figure, not a narrative.

13.event: Ravina, holding his orphaned nephew's wine, is taking his own wine to Sikhra to sell
13.turn: He asks Rav Ashi whether he may take the orphan's wine too
13.outcome: Rav Ashi tells him to go
13.summary: Ravina held wine belonging to his orphaned nephew and was taking his own wine to Sikhra. He asked Rav Ashi whether he could bring the orphan's along, and Rav Ashi told him to go, since it was no better than his own.
13.missing: Any stated outcome after the ruling.
13.reason: There is an actual undertaking (transporting wine) and a ruling, but the change is only implied; leaning borderline over not.

14.event: He found a lineage scroll in Jerusalem
14.summary: Shimon ben Azzai reports finding a genealogical scroll in Jerusalem, listing a mamzer, praise of R. Eliezer ben Yaakov's teaching, and that Manasseh killed Isaiah.
14.missing: Any response or consequence of the find.
14.reason: A single act (finding a scroll) reported as evidence of its contents, with nothing following, is a bare report.

15.missing: The incident itself; only Rabbi's award of one-twelfth is cited, then analysed.
15.reason: An incident reduced to a ruling and cited as proof in legal discussion has no narrated action or change.

16.missing: Any event beyond a document coming before a rabbi and a correction in speech.
16.reason: A case before a rabbi, his inclination and a colleague's correction are speech and ruling only, with no conflict beyond ordinary scholarly correction.

17.actor: Rav Kahana; Mar bar Rav Ashi
17.event: Rav Kahana took a cloth for a redemption, valuing it at five sela; Mar bar Rav Ashi overpaid for a cloth
17.summary: Rav Kahana accepted a cloth for redeeming a firstborn, saying it was worth five sela to him. Mar bar Rav Ashi bought a cloth worth ten for thirteen.
17.missing: Any response or consequence; both are one-line precedents.
17.reason: Two bare reports of what someone did, cited as evidence in a legal argument, with nothing following.

18.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and his sons
18.event: On his deathbed Rabbi summons his younger son, then his older son
18.turn: He transmits wisdom to Shimon and the office of Nasi to Gamliel
18.outcome: Rabban Gamliel is charged to lead with firmness
18.summary: Dying, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi asked for his younger son; Rabbi Shimon came in and received the orders of wisdom. Then he asked for his older son; Rabban Gamliel came in, received the procedures of the patriarchate, and was told to lead assertively.
18.reason: Part of the deathbed narrative with successive actions (summoning, entering, transmitting) and a change of leadership.

19.actor: A certain man; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
19.event: A man testifies another has Levite status because he read second in synagogue
19.turn: R. Yehoshua ben Levi questions him and he adds that a priest read first
19.outcome: R. Yehoshua ben Levi elevates the man to Levite status
19.summary: A man came before R. Yehoshua ben Levi testifying that someone was a Levite since he read second in the synagogue. Questioned, he explained a priest had read before him, and R. Yehoshua ben Levi elevated the man to Levite status.
19.missing: Any action beyond the testimony, questioning and the ruling.
19.reason: Mostly a case before a rabbi with questioning, but the ruling is itself an act changing someone's status, like the apportioning in Ketubot 65a, which keeps it borderline.

20.missing: Any event; it is a question and a cryptic wordplay answer.
20.reason: A question and a clever reply is speech without conflict or event.
